requirements.text: The central trading system (CTS) is to complete the trading of stock.
It analyses the instructions that enter the central trading system and divides them into several kinds of instructions.
System will make a match between them under specifically prescripts.
Also central trading system provides some interfaces to send messages to other modules.
The CTS receive instructions from trade client serve.
Then the CTS produce new messages which to be sent to network message promulgating after deal with the instructions from trade client serve.
The CTS provides the terminal users easy Operations that are confined to a series of mouse clicks and keyboard.
The CTS will match the instructions with the same stock id.
The CTS will make a trade by matching.
The CTS will modify the information of matched instructions.
The CTS will cancel the correlative instruction.
The CTS will give out the successful trade information.
The CTS will implement the query.
The CTS will structuralize the queried data.
The CTS will send the data to release.
The CTS will freeze the fund of user’s account.
The CTS will reject a trading instruction if the trading price is higher than the rising limit or lower than the falling limit.
The CTS will return the result to the client serve for any trading instructions that go into the CTS.
If an instruction hasn’t finished its trading in one day, it will be removed from the CTS.

The system shall implement role-based access control (RBAC) for all interfaces, encrypt all sensitive trading data at rest and in transit using AES-256 or equivalent, and maintain an immutable audit log of all instruction modifications.
All system logs shall be stored in a tamper-evident format, protected from unauthorized modification, and retained for a minimum of [X] years to comply with financial auditing standards.
The system shall process at least 10,000 trade instructions per second with a maximum latency of 50ms per transaction.
The system shall maintain a persistent, immutable audit log of all incoming instructions and state transitions to support fault recovery and forensic analysis.
The system shall process at least 5,000 trade instructions per second with a 99th percentile latency of less than 50ms.
The system shall return trade confirmation to the Transaction User Interface within 200ms of the match execution.

OPEN: The PRD mentions that the system manager is authorized to access information in the CTS but does not define the scope of this authorization or the mechanism for verifying identity. - The system shall enforce strict authentication for the system manager and limit access to only the data necessary for operational maintenance, logging all access attempts.

OPEN: The PRD identifies that the system must handle crashes but does not define recovery time objectives (RTO) or recovery point objectives (RPO). - The system shall achieve an RTO of less than 30 seconds and an RPO of zero for all confirmed trade instructions in the event of a system failure.

OPEN: The PRD mentions 'all the operations have been suspended' as an exception but does not define the system's behavior during partial failures or network partitions. - The system shall implement a circuit breaker pattern for external subsystem communications and ensure data consistency via transactional integrity during partial service outages.

OPEN: The PRD does not specify the expected number of concurrent users or the total volume of instructions the system must support. - The system shall support a minimum of 10,000 concurrent active trading sessions and a daily volume of 1,000,000 instructions.
